overall: The AG found one violation: the November 10 open-session notice was insufficiently specific because it did not identify the superintendent as the subject of the complaints. All other allegations were rejected, and no intentional violation was found.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee refused to reschedule an October 26 executive session after the superintendent's attorney could not attend, violating the right to counsel.
allegations.key_passage: Next, the Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to accommodate the schedule of a Purpose 1 subject’s attorney when scheduling an executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the October 26 executive session discussed professional competence, which is not a proper executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: We find that, taken as a whole, the Committee’s discussions on October 26 were appropriate for executive session

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 10 notice excluded professional competence, yet the committee discussed it, and that the October 26 and November 10 notices were insufficient on this point.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons explained above, we find that the discussion focused on the complaints and not professional competence independent of the complaints, and therefore the notices were sufficient in this regard.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee improperly amended the November 10 notice within 48 hours to strike 'executive session' and add 'open session'.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it later amended the notice to clarify that the meeting would be conducted in open session, not executive session.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee improperly added a 'Public Comment' topic to the November 10 notice within 48 hours of the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Public comment is not itself a topic for the public body’s discussion that needs to be listed on the meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session topic failed to say whether the discussion concerned reputation, discipline, complaints or charges.
allegations.key_passage: We find that where the notice topic specified “complaint relative to administrator,” the notice was sufficiently specific in this regard.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the November 10 notice topic was insufficiently specific because it did not identify the superintendent as the subject of the discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by including an insufficiently specific topic on the notice for the November 10 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to give sufficient notice that the November 10 meeting location changed from the Town Building room to the high school lecture hall.
Complaint alleged committee members deliberated outside a posted meeting in adding employee-evaluation complaints to the scope of the investigation between October 26 and November 10.
allegations.key_passage: we find no evidence that the Committee deliberated outside of a properly noticed meeting

allegations.summary: Complainant urged that the notice violation was intentional, which would carry a higher penalty under the law.
allegations.key_passage: but we do not find evidence that the Committee acted intentionally to violate the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
